1: Andre is 1-0 and got there the boring way, 139.14 behind 27.4 from David Montgomery and 27.2 from Justin Jefferson. The 86 Cokeboys are also 1-0, though the fine print reads that their 107.70 beat a team that scored 51.02, the lowest total in the league by a comfortable margin. The expansion side now learns the difference between clearing the floor and clearing the bar. Winner: Andre
2: Sunday's low-water mark belongs to Micah, whose 51.02 featured a Houston defense that finished at minus four and 0.7 from Jaylen Waddle. He responded by spending 25 FAAB on tight end Justin Joly, which is either conviction or a distress signal. Jared arrives 0-1 despite 37.26 from Caleb Williams and 29.7 from Ashton Jeanty, and he trails this series 1-3 all time, so treat this as the week the arithmetic finally cooperates. Winner: Jared
3: Two teams enter at 0-1 and one of them has to leave with a win, which the schedule makers consider a feature. Stop, It Hurts! produced 69.52 in the opener, a figure that included 0.8 from Mason Taylor and 4.1 from Davante Adams. YOUR TEAM IS ASS lost by 5.94 while starting a tight end who managed 2.3, and the all-time series between these two sits at 1-1. Somebody's season starts Sunday; the other one begins its descent. Winner: Stop, It Hurts!
4: The commissioner is 1-0 and will be unbearable about it. Chris posted 135.46 on 35.66 from Josh Allen and 18.5 from DJ Moore, a player he acquired by trade from this week's opponent, which is the sort of detail that ruins a Thanksgiving. Bourne to Nailor won its opener 79.70 to 73.76, the lowest winning score of the week, on Christian Watson's 29.7 and very little else. Winner: Chris
5: Dan scored 150.56 in Week 1 and lost. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 31.1, Jonathan Taylor added 23.6, Amon-Ra St. Brown 23.7, and the return on all of it was the second-highest total in the league and an 0-1 record. Edwin advanced the ordinary way, 124.46 with 21 from the Pittsburgh defense and one entire point from Brandon Aubrey, and now meets a team he is 4-4 against all time and that is furious in a way the standings cannot express. Winner: Dan
6: Nobody outscored Corey last week. The 158.46 came from 34.8 by Derrick Henry, 31.9 by D'Andre Swift, and 19 from Evan McPherson, a kicker he claimed off waivers for zero dollars after releasing Tyler Loop. Kevin's 115.90 was undone by 2.2 from Ja'Marr Chase, though he does hold a 5-2 edge in this matchup all time, which is the only sentence in this preview that favors him. Winner: Corey
